title: Purpose of the instanceof operator
answer: The `instanceof` operator checks whether an object reference is compatible with a specified reference type at runtime. It returns `true` when the object can be treated as that type and `false` otherwise; `null instanceof SomeType` is always `false`. It is commonly used before type-specific logic or casting. With modern Java pattern matching, `value instanceof String text` performs the type check and, when it succeeds, creates a safely typed pattern variable without a separate cast.

steps.title: Start from type-based behavior already used in AeroTopo
steps.question: AeroTopo already chooses behavior according to an object's runtime type inside `LanguageLab.format`, using Java's modern pattern-matching switch. Before introducing `instanceof` directly, inspect this method and identify why runtime type information matters when one `Object` parameter can receive Integer, String, null, or another object.
steps.why_te: LanguageLab.format lo `Object` value runtime type batti different branch select avutundi. Integer, String, null ki separate behavior undi. `instanceof` kuda runtime type compatibility ni check cheyyadaniki use avutundi.

steps.title: Create a direct instanceof experiment
steps.question: A direct `instanceof` example makes the operator's contract easier to see than a switch expression alone. The temporary class checks a String pattern, an Integer pattern, and then falls back for null or another object. Which part of this code proves that the operator can combine a runtime type test with a typed pattern variable?
steps.why_te: Temporary demo lo String mariyu Integer kosam `instanceof` pattern use chestunnam. Condition true ayithe `label` leda `count` typed variable automatic ga available avutundi. Separate cast rayalsina avasaram taggutundi.

steps.title: Inspect the String pattern variable
steps.question: The expression `value instanceof String label` first checks whether the runtime object is compatible with String and only then introduces `label` as a String. Why is this safer and clearer than performing an unchecked cast first, especially when the method accepts the broad `Object` type?
steps.why_te: Highlight ayina condition first runtime type ni check chestundi. Match true ayithe `label` already String type lo available avutundi. Wrong object ni direct ga String cast chese risk ikkada avoid avutundi.

target.expected_text: if (value instanceof String label) return "String:" + label.strip();

steps.title: Compare another type and the null fallback
steps.question: The next branch tests Integer, while the fallback explicitly handles null. Java defines every `null instanceof Type` expression as false, so null reaches the fallback instead of either pattern branch. How do these neighboring lines show both type compatibility testing and the operator's null-safe boolean behavior?
steps.why_te: Integer object vaste second `instanceof` branch match avutundi. `null` అయితే String leda Integer branch match kaadu; condition false avutundi. Anduke null check fallback lo handle chestunnam.

target.expected_text: if (value instanceof Integer count) return "Integer:" + count;

steps.title: Run String, Integer, and null through the operator
steps.question: One execution can now exercise three different runtime values through the same `Object` parameter. When the program prints a String result, an Integer result, and then `null`, what evidence does that give you about `instanceof` selecting only compatible type branches without throwing for the null reference?
steps.why_te: Program three values ni same method ki pass chestundi. String and Integer correct branches select avutayi; null fallback ki velthundi. `instanceof` null meeda exception throw cheyyakunda false return chestundi.
